ev: Left to the build: the N-input fold, the flag's threading, a cycle guard and a dedup for the fold, and enumeration in the resolver.
All four landed: merge.rs:169 fold_sources; merge.rs:197-203 the any_replace flag; use_graph.rs:84 source_fold_order plus pipeline/fold.rs:97 the include guard; resolver/glob.rs:60 expand_pattern.

RE-DERIVED after the build, not inherited: the prior verdict judged a plan and carried its own SELF-JUDGED caveat asking a later reviewer to re-derive. The status flip @spec/plan -> @impl/done is earned by four addresses that now exist and are named above.
One new entry point fold_sources(contract, &[sources]), with fold_source(c, s) kept as the degenerate fold_sources(c, &[s]) so every existing fold test is the regression harness.

merge.rs:169 fold_sources; merge.rs:242-244 fold_source delegating to fold_sources(contract, &[source]); test fold_source_equals_fold_sources_singleton at merge.rs:484 byte-compares the two entry points across the matched, add, contract-only and source-only branches.

The kept name did the job it was kept for: the prior verdict called the existing tests a real regression harness for a generalisation not yet written, and the singleton-equality test is that harness made explicit.

The per-section rule over a sequence: S(a) empty -> contract section whole; any member carrying :replace -> drop the contract text and emit the members in order; otherwise contract text minus every fact any member redeclares, then the members.

merge.rs:194 the empty branch; merge.rs:197-199 any_replace; merge.rs:200-203 the replace branch; merge.rs:204-212 the add branch via overridden_facts and text_without; merge.rs:224-234 the source-only append. Tests merge.rs:408 (add order), :421 (replace on the second source), :438 (union of overridden facts), :502 (empty slice).
Each of the three branches the design named maps onto an arm that now exists, and each arm carries its own test rather than sharing one.
The delta from the single-source law is two words, 'any' and 'every': one source becomes a sequence, and fact-override becomes a union over that sequence.

'any': merge.rs:197 members.iter().any(...) so one :replace suffices, pinned by fold_sources_replace_on_second_keeps_both_sources at merge.rs:421. 'every': the union at merge.rs:147-151 inside overridden_facts, applied at merge.rs:207, pinned by fold_sources_add_union_of_overridden_facts at merge.rs:438.
The claim that nothing else about the section rule moves survives the build: the branch structure of the pre-B-056 fold is unchanged, and the two words are the only widenings.

The dropped fact set is the union over all sources; a fact redeclared by two sources at once is not a fold problem, because both redeclarations survive into the merged text and the anchor-uniqueness recheck fails on the duplicate.

merge.rs:142-158 overridden_facts, union by flat_map into a HashSet at :147-151, applied at :207; the surviving-duplicate half at gate.rs:54 first_duplicate, pinned end to end by a_fact_duplicate_between_two_sources_fails_the_build at pipeline/fold_tests.rs:182.

This fact's reliance on the post-merge gate SURVIVES where its neighbour's did not, and the difference is exactly the gate's rule: first_duplicate fires when a FACT sits on either side of the repeat (gate.rs:64), so a doubly-redeclared fact trips it. What does not trip it is a heading-only repeat, which is fold-source-only-collision's business and not this fact's.
A source-only anchor declared by two sources IS an error, and the asymmetry against a source section matching a contract anchor is deliberate: declaration is idempotent, definition is not.

The catcher is pipeline/fold.rs:173 first_source_section_collision -> CompileError::DuplicateSourceSection (pipeline.rs:60-66), detector at pipeline/fold.rs:211 flagging two or more distinct members per source-only anchor; test two_sources_defining_one_source_only_section_fails_even_without_a_fact at pipeline/collision_tests.rs:24, with the legal mirror at :61 and the inner-level naming at :113.

EVIDENCE REPLACED, and the replacement is the point of this re-judgement. The claim is unchanged and still holds, but the prior verdict named doctree.rs duplicate_anchors() as the mechanism that fails, and that mechanism does NOT fire here: gate.rs:64 tolerates a pure heading-vs-heading repeat by design, pinned by a_repeated_section_heading_is_not_flagged at gate.rs:131. A verdict whose claim survives on different evidence is not a re-affirmation, and this row is the reason the ten were re-read rather than re-stamped.
Order is declaration order, a glob is sorted before it joins, and the composed document is therefore a pure function of (tree, lockfile) rather than of filesystem enumeration order.

use_graph.rs:200-217 source_addresses walks Directives::parse top to bottom and flattens each expansion in place; resolver/glob.rs:109 sorts by (name, slot) before addresses are built, with dedup at :113. Tests: sources_fold_in_declaration_order_not_alphabetical at pipeline/fold_tests.rs:120, source_fold_preserves_declaration_order at use_graph.rs:457, and g2_sort_independent_of_creation_order at resolver/glob.rs:282.

The determinism argument the prior verdict accepted on the strength of a ruling plus a lockfile is now carried by code: the sort exists, and a test creates the slots in the wrong order on purpose to prove the result does not follow creation order.
The fold needs its own traversal over #source edges with the same three colours and the same is_contract predicate, reusing the existing walker rather than writing a second one.

use_graph.rs:84 source_fold_order calls the SAME visit body at use_graph.rs:102 that topo_order_from (:57) uses, parameterised by EdgeKind (:46-51); is_contract is the one predicate at :223. Pinned by source_edges_and_use_edges_do_not_mix at use_graph.rs:526, with the cycle rulings at :482 (contract cycle admitted) and :501 (impl-touching cycle rejected).

The one-implementation requirement was the fact's whole point and it is met literally: there is one visit, not two walkers agreeing by convention. The gap the prior verdict measured between use_graph.rs and merge.rs is closed by parameterisation rather than by a copy.
The glob adds exactly one capability: the resolver enumerating installed packages by pattern instead of resolving one coordinate, with everything downstream being the sequence fold.

resolver/glob.rs:60 expand_pattern (slot scan at :84, name match at :141, membership = name matched AND the document present at :121-128, sort at :109); downstream the members are flattened by source_addresses (use_graph.rs:196) and folded by the ordinary fold_source_closure. Tests g1_two_matches_in_name_order at resolver/glob.rs:264 and a_glob_source_folds_all_its_members_in_sorted_order at pipeline/tests.rs:344.
The claim's sharp edge - that nothing downstream is new - held: the glob path reaches the fold through the same edge reader as a pointed address, and no fold branch was added for it.

Build order, each step landable alone: fold_sources over an explicit list; the pipeline passing every #source in declaration order instead of .find(); the cycle guard and dedup over the extended walker; resolver enumeration, sorted.

Landed in that order over eight commits of 2026-08-05 (87bb2bc8, 68f03853, 16dd103a, bb1fd8eb, 1124cd4e, 38eba517, 5254f0cf). Step 2 is objectively complete: a grep for `.find(|d| d.kind == DirectiveKind::Source)` over crates/vibe-spec/src returns zero hits, and the pipeline now folds the whole closure at pipeline.rs:155.

The prior verdict confirmed a plan and noted that step 2 alone would close B-055; B-055 was in fact closed by that step (commit 77224fcf), so the ordering claim was load-bearing and correct rather than decorative.
